subject: Private deployment BYOK evidence & operator access approvals
messages:
From: Claire Morton <claire.morton@medsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence for BYOK and operator access – initial request

Hi Sofia / Marcus,

Thanks for walking us through the private deployment options earlier. Before procurement can move forward we need a concise set of artifacts that map responsibilities for customer-managed keys and explain operator access patterns. Specifically: 

- A one-page responsibility matrix that shows which party is the custodian of the CMK, who can perform key rotation, and which operations (decrypt/model-serving, backup retrieval, emergency break-glass) require customer approval.
- A network/dataflow diagram that highlights any telemetry or control-plane connections from Redwood operator tooling to the customer VPC/on-prem.
- Confirmation of whether Redwood ever stores or has access to unencrypted model input/output in persistent logs or backups (we assume no).
- A list of subprocessors that might be involved in support escalations or telemetry ingestion for private deployments.

From a legal perspective we also need proposed DPA language for: approval gating on operator key usage, onshore-only key escrow options for EU customers, and explicit audit evidence Redwood can provide (sample audit logs or SOC extracts).

Can you send the matrix + diagram and a short note addressing the four bullets by EOD Wednesday? If you have a redline DPA template we can review that in parallel that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Claire Morton
Sr. Counsel, MedSys Health
claire.morton@medsys.com

Subject: Re: Evidence for BYOK and operator access – initial request

Hi Claire — thanks for the list. Attaching two artifacts that should address most of your procurement asks: BYOK-responsibility-matrix.pdf and network-dataflow.svg. Quick answers inline below.

- Custody / Rotation: Customer holds the CMK in their KMS (BYOK). Redwood never imports or stores the plaintext key. We perform wrapping/unwrapping operations only at the request of the runtime; we do not persist unencrypted keys. Key rotation is performed by the customer KMS; Redwood will accept new key metadata via the established handshake API.
- Operator actions: Routine operational tasks (service health, model restarts) do not require key material. Break-glass operator actions (forensics or emergency model state recovery) are gated by a documented approval workflow: support engineer raises ticket -> customer-designated approver (SPOC) authorizes via signed artifact in the support portal -> temporary one-time decryption token is emitted that is auditable and time-limited.
- Persistent logs/backups: By default, PII/LLM input and generated outputs are not stored in plaintext in Redwood persistent backups for private deployments. We do retain structured telemetry (latency, model-id, token counts) and anonymized error traces. If you require zero-persistence of outputs we can enable stricter retention/ephemeral-mode in the deployment config.
- Subprocessors: For private deployments we use a short list of subprocessors for build and delivery only (artifact signing, on-prem software distribution); active telemetry/observability is routed to your VPC or a customer-managed telemetry sink where feasible. Full subprocessor list attached in the matrix.

Regarding DPA language, we have a redline we typically start from for BYOK customers — I can send a marked-up DPA with a proposed clause for operator-key usage approval and an optional onshore-escrow addendum for EU accounts. Attaching an initial draft redline (DPA-redline-MedSys.docx).

Attachments:
- BYOK-responsibility-matrix.pdf (pdf, 42KB)
- network-dataflow.svg (svg, 18KB)
- DPA-redline-MedSys.docx (docx, 55KB)

If helpful, Marcus and I can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the security team through the approval flow and telemetry boundaries.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morton <claire.morton@medsys.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for BYOK and operator access – initial request

Claire / Sofia — quick clarifications from an ops perspective: 

1) Break-glass provenance: we will only emit scoped keys/tokens after a documented approval action. That event produces an immutable audit entry (timestamp, approver id, justification) and the temporary credential is single-use and expires within 10 minutes by default. We can extend logging retention for customers to 90 days on request.

2) Key escrow / custody: Redwood does not hold CMKs in typical BYOK. For customers that insist on escrow we offer an optional escrow workflow: Redwood keeps an encrypted escrow blob (wrapped under a customer-owned escrow KEK) that can be released only with bylaw’d legal triggers and multi-party approval (customer + Redwood compliance). We have one reference implementation for this pattern used by a financial services customer; happy to share the audit trail for that engagement.

3) Subprocessors and remote support: The subprocessors involved in packaging/distribution do not have access to customer production key material. Telemetry ingestion is configurable — default routes to customer-managed sinks (recommended). We maintain a SCIM-like access model for support engineers; they do not get direct keystore access without the approval workflow described above.

4) Evidence/SOC2: we can provide SOC2 Type II excerpts that reference our controls around key management and support gating; we cannot share customer-specific logs but can provide templates and anonymized examples of the audit entries produced during a break-glass.

If you confirm the retention window and whether you want the escrow option documented in the DPA redline, I’ll prepare language for the procurement team.

—Marcus

From: Claire Morton <claire.morton@medsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T14:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Evidence for BYOK and operator access – initial request

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow ups and suggested DPA language to accelerate procurement: 

- Retention: 90 days retention for break-glass audit entries is acceptable. Please confirm the format (immutable event with ISO timestamp + approver identity + ticket id) and that those entries are exportable as a CSV/JSON for audit.
- Escrow: we will opt for the onshore-only key escrow addendum for the EU deployment. Can you add optional language that escrow blobs are wrapped under a customer-managed escrow KEK and that release requires both Redwood compliance sign-off and the customer SPOC?
- Subprocessors: please include the names and jurisdictions of the packaging/distribution subprocessors in the redline appendix.

Suggested DPA clause (copy/paste ready):
"Operator key usage. For Private Deployments where Customer elects BYOK, Contractor (Redwood) shall not persist Customer master key material in plaintext or use Customer key material for any purpose other than performing the services expressly described in this Agreement. Any emergency or support-related decryption or key usage shall require prior documented approval by a Customer-authorized approver via the mutually agreed support portal. Authorization events shall be logged immutably and retained for no less than ninety (90) days and made available to Customer upon reasonable request for audit purposes"

I attached a marked DPA redline with the escrow paragraph and a short appendix with counterparty names we need for our procurement committee. If you can confirm the exportability of the audit entries (CSV/JSON) and update the redline with an escrow-release workflow that requires dual-approval, procurement will take the DPA into legal review next week.

Appended attachments:
- DPA-redline-MedSys.docx (redline with suggested clause)
- procurement-audit-appendix.xlsx (list of internal committees we need to satisfy)

If you both are available Friday morning (PST) we can run through the redline live.

Best regards,
Claire Morton
Sr. Counsel, MedSys Health
claire.morton@medsys.com
